degenerate: The rule itself is that rare. It is not a plugin bug. (1) Funnel at k 1.0 in TTM's own blind build, written from the prereg text alone: 1550 sessions -> 1550 long enough -> 1549 with ATR(14) defined -> 1 quiet -> 1 signal -> 1 trade. The plugin, the frozen own_rule and an independent pandas recount all find the same single session. (2) The ratio of the 12-bar range to ATR(14) at session bar 11, over 1549 sessions: median 3.11, 10th percentile 2.11, 1st 1.57, 0.1th 1.30, minimum 0.85. Only one session falls at or below 1.0: Labor Day 2015-09-07, a thin 103-bar holiday session with a 4.5-pt range against an ATR of 5.29. That ATR was pumped up by a 34-pt overnight gap in the first bar's true range (the three outside bars' true ranges sum to 50.75). (3) Why it is structurally near-impossible: each true range of session bars 1..11 is at most the 12-bar range (checked in all 1549 sessions). So range <= 1.0 x ATR(14) needs the 3 bars outside that set (the prior session's last 2 bars, plus the first bar with its gap) to sum to at least 3x the range. The median of that sum is 1.28x the range. 139 sessions pass this necessary condition and only 1 passes the full test. A 12-bar range is about sqrt(12), roughly 3.5x, a one-bar ATR on a random walk, so k = 1.0 asks for an opening that barely moves. (4) Units are points vs points, the session filter passes 1550/1550, there are no ties at 1.0, and no off-by-one changes the count: TTM's independent build agrees exactly. (5) Rate by compress_k, same in my build and the plugin's: 0.16/yr at 1.0 and 1.25, 1.6 at 1.5, 6.9 at 1.75, 18.8 at 2.0 (the file maximum), 58 at 2.5, 113 at 3.0. Reaching the prior's 120/yr needs k of about 3.1, outside the file's 0.5-2.0 range. Root cause: a design error in the idea. The default compress_k of 1.0 scales a 12-bar range against a single bar's ATR. The model's 120 trades/yr prior implicitly assumes k near 3.
